newsitem.title: USA: Northeast sees a Millstone unit up by end-97.
newsitem.headline: Northeast sees a Millstone unit up by end-97.

text.p: Northeast Utilties CEO Bruce Kenyon said Wednesday that the company expects to be able to reopen one of the nuclear units at its Millstone power station by the end of this year.
"I continue to believe we can restart one unit by the end of this year," Kenyon said at a briefing to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

The company last week said that it planned to have Millstone Unit 3 ready for restart by September and Millstone Unit 2 ready by November. All three Millstone nuclear units have been closed for safety reasons since March 1996.
Kenyon stressed that "ready to restart ... does not mean that the NRC will have completed all that it needs to do to evaluate what we have done."
NRC commissioners scolded Northeast for failing to provide enough information for them to judge the company's progress in solving major safety problems at the Waterford, Conn. plant.

"It's important ... that the commission hears about where you actually are and results, because it is the commission in the end that's going to have to take the vote (to approve a restart)," NRC Chairwoman Shirley Jackson said.

Commissioners at the second quarterly review of Millstone's progress said the company needed to provide more specific information for them to be able to eventually make a decision on whether to approve reopening of any of the units.
"I'm definitely not pleased with the amount of specific information that was provided," Commissioner Nils Diaz said.
"I'd like to see a real engineering-in-progress assessment of where you are. We don't have that," he said.
NRC staff said that the company was still in the very early stages of improving its operations.
"Their program is not far enough along for ours to begin to initiate any of the very significant inspections," said Bill Travers, director of the NRC's Special Projects Office.
But he added that regulators had seen "positive action in a number of areas," including improvements in quality assurance and prioritization of engineering problems.
